instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.62(11) defines a lobbyist as any individual employed by, contracting for, or receiving economic consideration (beyond actual-expense reimbursement) from a principal whose duties include lobbying — no minimum dollar amount is set, so any paid person qualifies (YES/Tier 0).

The lobbyist definition in § 13.62(11) contains no expenditure threshold for the lobbyist's own spending that triggers registration; lobbyist status is based on receiving compensation for lobbying, not on dollars spent.

Section 13.64(1) requires registration only when a principal's lobbying expenditures/obligations exceed $500 in a calendar year, and § 13.621(5) allows a principal anticipating no more than $500 in such expenditures to file a verified statement exempting it from licensing, registration, and expense-reporting requirements.

Neither the lobbyist definition in § 13.62(11) nor the reporting provisions of § 13.68(1)(a) establish a percentage-of-compensated-time exemption from lobbyist filing duties; the only time-related carve-out is a flat 10-hours-per-reporting-period rule for non-lobbyist employees in expense aggregation, not a percentage-based filing exemption for the lobbyist.

content.text:
I'll analyze each cell against the Wisconsin statute text.

**row_001**: Lobbyist definition — § 13.62(11) defines lobbyist as one who "contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses, from a principal." No dollar threshold on the lobbyist side; any paid person is a lobbyist (subject to the 5-day rule if duties aren't exclusively lobbying).

**row_002**: No expenditure threshold on the lobbyist's own spending triggers lobbyist status. The $500 threshold in § 13.64(1) applies to the principal's registration, not lobbyist definition.

**row_003**: § 13.62(11) — "the individual is a lobbyist only if he or she makes lobbying communications on each of at least 5 days within a reporting period" (only when duties aren't exclusively lobbying). This is a day-count threshold.

**row_004**: § 13.68(1)(a)5 — paid advertising etc. lobbying expenditures included only "if the total amount of all such lobbying expenditures made and obligations incurred exceeds $500 during the reporting period." § 13.68(1)(a)6 itemizes lobbyist payments only if exceeds $200. So not all expenditures must be itemized — there are de minimis thresholds.

**row_005**: § 13.621(5) and § 13.64(1) — principal exempted from full registration/reporting if expenditures don't exceed $500/calendar year (verified statement option).

**row_006**: § 13.68(1)(a) excludes from aggregate reporting "any employee of the principal who is not a lobbyist and who devotes not more than 10 hours to lobbying during a reporting period." This is an hours threshold, not a percentage of compensated time. No percentage-based threshold exists in the statute.

input.justification: Section 13.62(11) defines a lobbyist as any individual employed by, contracting for, or receiving economic consideration (beyond actual-expense reimbursement) from a principal whose duties include lobbying — no minimum dollar amount is set, so any paid person qualifies (YES/Tier 0).

The lobbyist definition in § 13.62(11) contains no expenditure threshold for the lobbyist's own spending that triggers registration; lobbyist status is based on receiving compensation for lobbying, not on dollars spent.

Section 13.62(11) provides that when an individual's duties are not exclusively lobbying, the individual is a lobbyist "only if he or she makes lobbying communications on each of at least 5 days within a reporting period," establishing a time/day-count threshold in the lobbyist definition.

Section 13.68(1)(a)5 requires reporting paid-advertising/grassroots lobbying expenditures only "if the total ... exceeds $500 during the reporting period," and § 13.68(1)(a)6 requires itemizing payments to a lobbyist only if they exceed $200 — both de minimis thresholds exempt lobbying expenditures below those amounts from individualized disclosure.

Section 13.64(1) requires registration only when a principal's lobbying expenditures/obligations exceed $500 in a calendar year, and § 13.621(5) allows a principal anticipating no more than $500 in such expenditures to file a verified statement exempting it from licensing, registration, and expense-reporting requirements.

Neither the lobbyist definition in § 13.62(11) nor the reporting provisions of § 13.68(1)(a) establish a percentage-of-compensated-time exemption from lobbyist filing duties; the only time-related carve-out is a flat 10-hours-per-reporting-period rule for non-lobbyist employees in expense aggregation, not a percentage-based filing exemption for the lobbyist.
